q: 1. A flooring made of 4 to 6 mm marble chips is known as ..........
explain: Mosaic flooring consists of small pieces (chips) of marble or colored stones arranged in patterns and set in mortar.

q: 2. The dadoring in bath room should be upto ..........
explain: In bathrooms, dado (wall tiling) is usually provided up to 2 meters (200 cm) to protect walls from water splashes.

q: 3. The ceiling height of a buildings is the height ..........
options: of the ceiling above ground level
of the roof above ground level
explain: Ceiling height is defined as the vertical distance measured from the finished floor level to the underside of the ceiling.

q: 4. The most extensively used type of pointing in brick and stone masonries is ..........
explain: Flush pointing is the most common because it is durable and does not provide a ledge for water or dust to accumulate.

q: 5. The type of pointing in which the mortar is first pressed into the raked joint and then finished off flush with the edges of the brick or stone is called ..........
explain: This describes the standard application of flush pointing, where the mortar is trimmed to match the face of the masonry.

q: 6. The type of pointing in which the mortar is first pressed into the raked joint and the face of the pointing is kept vertical and inside the plane of the wall by means of a suitable tool is called ..........
explain: In recessed pointing, the mortar is pushed back from the masonry face to create a shadow line and a decorative effect.

q: 7. The glass one side of which is patterned while rolling and which obscures the direct vision but does not obstruct light is known as ..........
explain: Figured glass (patterned glass) allows light to pass through while distorting the view for privacy.

q: 8. The narrow strips of wood or bands of plaster laid on the floor at intervals to act as guides for bringing the whole of the true and even surface are termed as ..........
explain: Screeds are narrow strips laid on a floor to act as gauges or guides for maintaining an even thickness and level surface of the concrete or mortar.

q: 9. The cheapest floor which remains warm in winter and cool in summer is ..........
explain: Mud flooring is inexpensive and possesses excellent thermal insulation properties, naturally regulating temperature throughout the seasons.

q: 10. A horizontal layer of bricks laid in mortar is known as ..........
explain: In masonry, a course is a single continuous horizontal layer of bricks or stones.

q: 11. The brick flooring may be done with bricks ..........
options: set at right angle to the walls
laid on edge arranged in herring-bone fashion
explain: Brick flooring is versatile; it can be laid flat, on edge, or in patterns like herring-bone for better aesthetics and strength.

q: 12. A type of flooring made with special aggregate of, marble chips mixed with white and coloured cement, is called ..........
explain: Terrazzo flooring consists of marble chips embedded in a cement binder, then ground and polished to a smooth finish.

q: 13. The horizontal upper part of a step on which for is placed in ascending or descending a stairway, is called ..........
explain: The tread is the flat, horizontal surface of a step where one places their foot.

q: 14. The brick flooring is used in ..........
explain: Due to its durability and low cost, brick flooring is frequently used in warehouses (godowns) and industrial sheds.

q: 15. The flooring made with small pieces of broken tiles of china glazed or of marble arranged in different pattern, is known as ..........
explain: Mosaic flooring involves using small pieces of tile, glass, or stone to create artistic patterns.

q: 16. In stairs, the flier is ..........
options: a vertical portion of a step providing a support to the tread
a straight step having a parallel width of tread
the under surface of a stair
the angle which the line of nosing of the stair makes with the horizontal
explain: A flier is an ordinary rectangular step in a flight that has a uniform width.

q: 17. In stairs, the soffit is ..........
options: a vertical portion of a step providing a support to the tread
a straight step having a parallel width of tread
the under surface of a stair
the angle which the line of nosing of the stair makes with the horizontal
explain: The soffit refers to the underside of a flight of stairs or an arch.

q: 18. The size of a step commonly adopted for residential buildings is ..........
explain: A tread of 270mm and a riser of 150mm is a standard comfortable ratio for residential use.

q: 19. The pointing which is extensively used in brick work and stone masonry face work, is ..........
explain: Struck pointing (where the upper edge is pressed in) is very common as it sheds water effectively and looks neat.

q: 20. The type of pointing in which the mortar is first pressed into the raked joints and then finished off flush with the edges of the bricks or stones, is called ..........
explain: Flush pointing is the simplest form, where the mortar is finished level with the face of the masonry.

q: 21. The type of pointing in which the mortar is first pressed into the raked joints and then finished off flush with the face of the bricks or stones, is called ..........
explain: In tuck pointing, a groove is made in the flush mortar and filled with a narrow strip of white putty to give the illusion of very fine joints.

q: 22. The brick arranged systematically and bedded together in mortar to form a homogeneous mass capable of withstanding and transmitting forces is known as ..........
explain: This is the general definition of brick masonry as a structural system.

q: 23. Generally while plastering in ordinary buildings, the ratio of cement and sand used in cement plaster should be ...........
explain: A 1:6 ratio (1 part cement to 6 parts sand) is standard for internal plastering on brick or stone walls.

q: 24. The roughening of solid background to provide suitable key for plastering is called ...........
explain: Hacking is the process of making small grooves or indents in a smooth surface (like concrete) so the plaster can bond effectively.

q: 25. Dislodgement of plaster work from the background is known as ...........
explain: Peeling occurs when the bond between the plaster and the wall fails, causing the plaster to fall off in layers.

q: 26. The surface to which the first coat of plaster is applied is called ...........
explain: The background surface is the bare masonry or concrete wall that receives the initial layer of plaster.

q: 27. The development of one or more local swelling on the finished plastered surface, is called ...........
explain: Blistering is a defect caused by the presence of unslaked lime or trapped air/moisture behind the plaster coat.

q: 28. Which of the following pointing is extensively used in brick work and stone masonry face work?
explain: Flush pointing is the most common because it is simple, durable, and does not provide a ledge for dust or water to collect.

q: 29. For pointing the masonry is raked out to a depth of about ...........
explain: To ensure a strong bond for the new mortar, joints should be raked to a depth of 15-20 mm before pointing.

q: 30. The development of a series of hair cracks on the finished surface, plastered usually in haphazard manner, is called ...........
explain: Crazing refers to fine network of cracks caused by shrinkage of the cement during drying, often due to excessive cement or rich mix.

q: 31. In a three coat plastering, the third coat known as ...........
explain: In three-coat work, the coats are: 1. Rendering coat, 2. Floating coat, and 3. Setting (or finishing) coat.

q: 32. Brick floors are used in ...........
explain: While used in many places, brick flooring is highly characteristic of railway platforms due to its durability and grip.

q: 33. In multistoried government buildings, the floor height is usually restricted to ...........
explain: A clear height of 3.4 meters is common in public/government buildings to allow for better ventilation and larger room sizes.

q: 34. The thickness of square or rectangular stones used in flagstone flooring varies from ...........
explain: Flagstones are usually 30mm to 50mm thick, providing a heavy-duty wearing surface.

q: 35. While laying cement concrete floor, the floor is divided into small panels. The length of the panel is restricted to ...........
explain: To prevent shrinkage cracks in large areas, concrete floors are laid in panels usually not exceeding 2 meters in length.

q: 36. For walls built in cement mortar 1:6, the minimum thickness for single storied building is ...........
explain: A standard 20 cm (9 inch) wall is the minimum requirement for load-bearing brickwork in a single-story building.

q: 37. The lime sand mortar normally used in brick construction has a ratio of ...........
explain: Lime mortar traditionally uses a richer 1:2 ratio (1 part lime to 2 parts sand) compared to cement mortars.

q: 38. The ratio of cement-sand mortar preferred in load bearing walls is ...........
explain: 1:6 cement mortar offers a good balance of strength and economy for load-bearing masonry.

q: 39. In jack arch floor, the rise given to the arch is ...........
explain: Jack arches are very shallow; the rise is typically kept to 1/12th of the span to minimize the vertical profile.
